The handoff says "keep the same allocation convention". That seems like a recommendation. But we must follow the shared objective: maximize distinct tasks, then minimize total cost. We must also respect tie-break rule: among rows that maximize distinct tasks and then minimize total cost, choose lexicographically smallest (A-task, B-task). So we need to evaluate possible A and B choices (simultaneously). Since we are only A, we need to pick a task that is part of a joint outcome that meets the objective and tie-break rule.

Then among those rows, minimize total cost across all four agents. Then among those, pick lexicographically smallest (A-task, B-task). Then we as A must choose the A-task from that pair.
